newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia's Reith sees more jobs, higher pay.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia's Reith sees more jobs, higher pay.

text.p: Australian Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith said on Wednesday the government's newly legislated labour reforms would lead to improved business efficiency and productivity.
"That means more jobs and higher wages for the people working in those businesses," Reith said on Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.

Late on Tuesday, parliament passed the government's controversial Workplace Relations Bill which deregulates the labour market and gives unions a less significant role in wage negotiations late on Tuesday. The changes are expected to take effect in February next year.
"What happened last night is not the end of the reform process," Reith said.
"It's the start of the practical implementation of the big changes that we've got in our bill."
He said reforms contained in the legislation, including secondary boycott provisions and abolition of the unfair dismissals scheme, were user-friendly and good for both employers and workers.
Reith said the Maritime Union of Australia's (MUA) pre-emptive strike on Tuesday in protest against the imminent passage of the bill showed why the legislation was needed.
"Now I must say, the MUA going out on strike last night is every good reason why we should have introduced the provisions we did," Reith said.
"They say it's a spontaneous reaction -- the truth of the matter is that they've had it planned for some time and this is exactly the way in which they operate," he said.
"This is exactly the reason why Australians have been losing jobs, productivity and income for years because of the MUA," Reith said.
